source: Wilf et al. (2023) Think Twice: Perspective-Taking Improves LLM Theory-of-Mind (SimToM)
finding: A two-stage prompt built on Simulation Theory: first filter the story to what the character knows, then answer. It beat zero-shot and zero-shot chain of thought on false-belief items for most models.
numbers: False-belief subset, SimToM vs 0-shot: Llama2-7b BigToM 70.5 vs 47.5; GPT-3.5 BigToM 70.5 vs 41.0, ToMI 81.0 vs 67.25; GPT-4 ToMI 87.75 vs 25.5 (0-shot) and 74.25 (CoT). All question types, ToMI: GPT-4 87.8 vs 66.5 (0-shot), 74.4 (CoT).
limits: BigToM and ToMI only. GPT-4 BigToM was near ceiling (92.0 vs 89.0 0-shot, CoT 93.25), so little gain there. Llama2-13b ToMI false belief went down 3.8 points vs 0-shot. Zero-shot; ToMI rewritten to give both answer choices. Table rows were realigned by me from garbled text and checked against the stated deltas.
agent_relevance: Cheapest known simulation-style scaffold: a separate perspective-filter call before answering. Fits our rule that the program decides steps and the model fills one slot.

source: Wilf et al. (2023) Think Twice: Perspective-Taking Improves LLM Theory-of-Mind (SimToM)
finding: Ablation: the perspective filter must be a separate call. Putting it in one prompt loses most of the gain, and asking for a rationale first is worse than doing nothing.
numbers: GPT-3.5, false belief (ToMI/BigToM): SimToM 81.0/70.5; SimToM-Single 58.75/50.75 (-22/-20); SimToM-Multi 31.75/37.25; domain-specific perspective-taking 85.5/90.5; oracle human perspective 96/96. All-types BigToM: SimToM 81.62, Single 54.75, Oracle 98.
limits: Only GPT-3.5 was ablated. Column order in the table-2 text extraction is ambiguous; values were matched to table 1.
agent_relevance: Perspective-taking quality is the bottleneck: with a perfect filtered story the model nearly solves the benchmark. Two separate calls beat one combined prompt, so a code-controlled hand-off is worth it.

source: Wilf et al. (2023) Think Twice: Perspective-Taking Improves LLM Theory-of-Mind (SimToM)
finding: Single-pass methods fail the same way: the model answers from the world state instead of the character's mental state. Tree-of-Thoughts also lost to SimToM.
numbers: Tree-of-Thoughts 33.50 on false-belief vs SimToM 81.00, as reported in the text.
limits: One model and one benchmark for the Tree-of-Thoughts comparison.
agent_relevance: Supports a rule that a belief question is answered from a filtered view, not the full context.

source: Kosinski (2023/2024) Evaluating large language models in theory of mind tasks (PNAS)
finding: 40 bespoke false-belief tasks (20 unexpected contents, 20 unexpected transfer) with controls. Success rose with model size, and was compared to children.
numbers: Solved: older models 0%; GPT-3-davinci-002 5%; GPT-3.5-turbo 20%; ChatGPT-4 (June 2023) 75% (CI95 66-84%), like 6-year-old children. Unexpected transfer: GPT-4 90%. Correlation between the two task types R=0.98.
limits: Single lab, hand-written items, scored by next-token probability. The paper does not frame results as simulation vs theory. Later work shows brittleness (c05, c06).
agent_relevance: A high average does not show robust belief tracking; test with perturbed items before trusting a ToM step.

source: Ullman (2023) Large Language Models Fail on Trivial Alterations to Theory-of-Mind Tasks
finding: Small changes that keep the ToM logic (for example transparent container, informed protagonist) turn GPT-3.5 results around. Argues failures outweigh averages.
numbers: Original Kosinski bag task: P(popcorn)=100% content prompt, P(chocolate)=99% first belief prompt, 82% second belief prompt. Altered versions gave the wrong belief.
limits: A small set of hand-made variants, not a large benchmark; GPT-3.5 mainly. Later GPT-4 passes some of them.
agent_relevance: Our test set for any ToM step should include trivial alterations that must not change the belief.

source: Shapira et al. (2023) Clever Hans or Neural Theory of Mind? Stress Testing Social Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Six-task stress test. Models do well on standard false-belief items but collapse on adversarial ones, consistent with shallow heuristics.
numbers: GPT-4 97% on the original false-belief subset but fails adversarial ones: transparent access fell from 66.7% (davinci-002) to 0% (GPT-4); 'inon' from 71.4% to 0%; 'other person' from 93.8% to 68.8%. Answers repeated across regenerations, so the errors are confident.
limits: GPT models mainly; MC-probing and LM-probing give slightly different numbers.
agent_relevance: Confident repeated errors mean agreement across samples is not evidence (matches our G4).

source: Gandhi et al. (2023) Understanding Social Reasoning in Language Models with Language Models (BigToM)
finding: BigToM: 25 controls and 5,000 model-written items built from causal templates. GPT-4 patterns most like humans; other models struggle, especially when the story states an initial belief.
numbers: Backward belief inference is hard even for humans: 82% accuracy (true belief), 72% (false belief). Most models far below chance on it. GPT-4 near human on forward belief and at human level on forward action zero-shot.
limits: Model-written items, two-choice. The authors note some earlier failures were perceptual-access errors, not ToM errors.
agent_relevance: BigToM is a usable template-built test bed; backward belief inference (what did she see?) is the hard slot.

source: Street et al. (2024) LLMs achieve adult human performance on higher-order theory of mind tasks
finding: Handwritten Multi-Order ToM Q&A (orders 2 to 6) against a large adult human sample. GPT-4 matches adults; Flan-PaLM is near adult level.
numbers: Human responses: 29,259 from UK adults. Overall GPT-4 vs humans chi2(1,N=280)=0.41, p=.522 (no difference); Flan-PaLM below humans p=.017. Humans better than GPT-4 only at order 5 (p=.0126); GPT-4 above adults at order 6. LaMDA answered 'true' to everything (50%).
limits: True/false statements on written stories, not interaction.
agent_relevance: Recursive belief depth is reachable by plain prompting with the best models; weaker models need external structure.

source: Wu et al. (2023) Hi-ToM: A Benchmark for Evaluating Higher-Order Theory of Mind Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Higher-order beliefs (zeroth to fourth) cause a steep accuracy loss; chain of thought gives small or no gain.
numbers: Joint accuracy goes from near perfect at order 0 to near zero at order 4. GPT-4 vanilla prompt 58.11 avg vs 59.88 with CoT (+1.77); GPT-3.5 27.50 vs 35.50 (+8.0).
limits: Story-based; detailed figures not all captured.
agent_relevance: Deep recursion is where plain models break; an explicit belief tracker is the natural fix (c10).

source: Sclar et al. (2023) SymbolicToM: plug-and-play multi-character belief tracker
finding: A decoding-time tracker keeps graph-structured belief states per character (and each character's belief about others) and feeds a filtered story to the model. Large zero-shot gains on ToMi.
numbers: Accuracy gains in points over the model alone across three question types: GPT-3.5 100 (+99), 100 (+99), 99 (+51); GPT-4 100 (+42), 100 (+38), 100 (+4); Macaw-3B 89 (+81), 71 (+60), 70 (+41); Flan-T5-XL 76 (-10), 96 (+46), 100 (+33).
limits: ToMi is template-based, so symbolic tracking is easy. Needs the story as entity-event structure. I did not map columns to question-type names.
agent_relevance: Closest published match to our program-controlled agent: code holds who-knows-what, the model only answers over the filtered view. A theory-style (explicit rules) plus simulation-style (filtered view) hybrid.

source: Kim et al. (2023) FANToM: stress-testing machine ToM in information-asymmetric conversations
finding: Conversation-based test with several question types that need the same reasoning, to expose an illusory ToM. All LLMs far below humans even with chain of thought.
numbers: Short context, ALL* score: Human 87.5; GPT-4-0613 + CoT 26.6 (June run) and 14.8 (October run); ChatGPT 3.7; Llama-2 chat 0.4; fine-tuned Flan-T5-XL 53.7.
limits: ALL* requires every question type for a fact to be right. Fine-tuning raised scores but the authors do not call that ToM.
agent_relevance: Consistency across question types is the right test, not single accuracy; measure belief consistency.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) How Far Are LLMs from Agents with Theory-of-Mind? (T4D, Foresee and Reflect)
finding: Thinking for Doing: models must choose an action from observations without being told which mental inference to make. GPT-4 reached 50%; a zero-shot scaffold (Foresee: predict the others' future actions and challenges; Reflect: choose the helpful action) raised it to 71%.
numbers: GPT-4 50% to 71% with FaR; human annotators over 95% agreement; FaR improved zero-shot performance by as much as 50% over CoT, Self-Ask and Tree-of-Thoughts.
limits: One task family, story form; FaR is sensitive to noisy foresight steps.
agent_relevance: FaR is a prospection plus simulate-the-other step usable inside an agent loop.

source: Sap et al. (2022) Neural Theory-of-Mind? On the Limits of Social Intelligence in LLMs
finding: GPT-3 lacks social intelligence out of the box on SocialIQa and ToMi.
numbers: Accuracy 55% and 60% (best setups), well below human (over 30% gap on SocialIQa); going from 10 to 35 in-context examples raised accuracy about 1 point.
limits: GPT-3 era; later models improve. Argues scale alone is not enough.
agent_relevance: Baseline from before reasoning models; shows how fast the field moved.

source: Rabinowitz et al. (2018) Machine Theory of Mind (ToMnet)
finding: A meta-learned neural observer predicts other agents' behaviour from past trajectories and passes a gridworld Sally-Anne style false-belief test. The authors cite simulation (Gordon; Gallese and Goldman) and Bayesian ToM (Baker) and say they do not directly implement either.
numbers: Agents: random, algorithmic, deep-RL species; held-out agents predicted after few observations; false-belief swap-event gridworld.
limits: Gridworld only; belief is not reported explicitly, only action predictions.
agent_relevance: A learned third path beyond simulation or theory: ToM as a prior over agent types.

source: Jin et al. (2024) MMToM-QA: Multimodal Theory of Mind Question Answering (BIP-ALM)
finding: Theory-based Bayesian inverse planning with a language model as the likelihood beats GPT-4(V) on belief and goal inference, below humans. GPT-4 fails false-belief and updated-belief goal items.
numbers: Overall: Human 93.0 (multimodal), 82.5 (text); GPT-4V 44.0; GPT-4 text 48.0; GPT-3.5 38.3; BIP-ALM with GPT-J 75.3. False belief (type 1.2): GPT-4 12.0, GPT-4V 13.0, BIP-ALM 69.0. Goal given updated belief (2.3): GPT-4 2.7, GPT-4V 4.0.
limits: Synthetic household environment; BIP-ALM needs symbolic state extraction.
agent_relevance: Explicit generative model of agents (goals, beliefs, planning) with LLM likelihoods outperformed pure prompting: a theory-theory style design.

source: Kim et al. (2025) Hypothesis-Driven Theory-of-Mind Reasoning for LLMs (ThoughtTracing, COLM 2025)
finding: Sequential Monte Carlo style inference-time loop: generate hypotheses about an agent's mental state at each step and weight them by later observations. Improves models on all four benchmarks with no question-specific input.
numbers: ParaphrasedToMi avg: GPT-4o 59.5, +CoT 67.0, +TT 76.0, +TT+CoT 74.3; o1-preview 68.0; DeepSeek R1 68.3. FANToM AllQs: GPT-4o 11.1, +CoT 40.7, +TT 41.5, +TT+CoT 54.7. MMToM-QA avg GPT-4o 56.5, +TT 60.0, +TT+CoT 69.0 (goal sub-score fell from 56.1 with CoT to 37.8 with TT).
limits: Gains uneven: Qwen 2.5 did not improve on FANToM with TT alone. Compared to my other lines, this paper is the clearest theory-style hypothesis loop.
agent_relevance: Hypothesis generate-and-weight is a theory-theory style loop (child as scientist) with code-side weighting; usable in our agent.

source: Kim et al. (2025) ThoughtTracing: reasoning-model behaviour on ToM
finding: Reasoning models (o1, o3-mini, R1) are not uniformly better at ToM. They pass false-belief items but fail true-belief controls, and extra effort did not always help.
numbers: o1-preview ParaphrasedToMi false belief 100.0 but true belief 36.0; o1-high-effort 97.0 / 49.0; GPT-4o 38.5 / 80.5; DeepSeek R1 77.0 / 59.5.
limits: One benchmark; error pattern attributed by the authors to over-suspecting false belief.
agent_relevance: Guard against a model that always assumes someone is mistaken: pair every false-belief test with a true-belief control.

source: Chen et al. (2024) ToMBench: Benchmarking Theory of Mind in LLMs
finding: Eight tasks and 31 abilities, multiple choice, bilingual, built from scratch to avoid contamination. Best LLMs still about 10 points under humans; GPT-4 beats humans on false belief only.
numbers: Human 85.4% vs GPT-4-1106 75.3% (task view); Human 86.1% vs GPT-4-0613 + CoT 75.3% (ability view). GPT-4-1106 above humans on the false-belief task.
limits: CoT gave mixed results across models in their tables.
agent_relevance: The gap lies in abilities beyond the classic false-belief test.

source: Gu et al. (2026, ICLR) SimpleToM: Exposing the gap between explicit ToM inference and applied ToM
finding: Models infer mental state well but fail to use it to predict behaviour or judge it.
numbers: 1147 items per question type. Mental state: GPT-4o 95.6, Llama-3.1-405B 97.8, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 97.9. Behaviour prediction: 49.5 / 58.2 / 67.0. Judgment: 15.3 / 10.0 / 24.9. o1-preview behaviour 84.1. GPT-3.5: 36.5 / 7.6 / 29.1.
limits: Binary questions, chance 50%, so some models score far below chance on judgment. Humans are more consistent across question types per the appendix.
agent_relevance: Our schema should force use of the inferred belief in the next step (code passes it in), because the model will not do it on its own.

source: Gu et al. (2026, ICLR) SimpleToM interventions
finding: A mental-state reminder (put the model's own earlier belief answer back in the prompt) closes most of the behaviour-prediction gap; a generic system prompt and chain of thought do not.
limits: Three models only. Judgment stays low for GPT-4o and Llama even with the reminder.
agent_relevance: A code-inserted 'what does she know' line before the action question is a cheap, large-effect scaffold (+33 points GPT-4o on behaviour).

source: Riemer et al. (2024/2025) Position: Theory of Mind Benchmarks are Broken for LLMs
finding: Introduces functional theory of mind: adapting to a partner in context. Literal ToM scores (predicting the other's behaviour) do not imply functional ToM.
numbers: No LLM came close to a tabular frequency-count baseline on functional regret in the repeated-game tests; instruction tuning tended to lower literal ToM but raise functional ToM (Mixtral above LLaMA-2 in one comparison).
limits: Simple partner policies, mostly open models; I did not capture the numeric regret table.
agent_relevance: Measure our agent on adapting to a partner over turns, not only on one-shot belief questions.

source: Aoki and Kawahara (2025) Testing Simulation Theory in LLMs' Theory of Mind (IJCNLP-AACL SRW)
finding: First direct mechanistic test of simulation theory in LLMs. They fit a linear map from a false-belief representation to a perspective-taking representation and intervene on hidden states; the answer flips toward the character's view in later layers.
numbers: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct answered 198 of 200 false-belief BigToM items correctly and Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct 196 of 200. Net intervention effect rises in later layers (Figure 4 at layer 75 of 80). Flip proportion stays small compared with the ideal of 1; regularization between 1e-4 and 1e-2 needed. I did not capture the exact peak value.
limits: 200 items, 2 models, linear-map assumption. Authors say simulation explains the mechanism only partially and heuristics may also be at work.
agent_relevance: Weak mechanistic evidence that the model builds a character-view representation, which supports explicit perspective prompts.

source: Thiyagarajan et al. (2025) UniToMBench: Integrating Perspective-Taking to Improve Theory of Mind in LLMs
finding: Combines SimToM prompts with ToMBench tasks. SimToM helped OpenAI models on multi-interaction, pretend-play and implicit-knowledge tasks but hurt Llama 3 8B and Gemma 2 27B on evolving stories, where models gave all agents the same knowledge.
numbers: Over 1,000 hand-written scenarios; GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4o, GPT-4o Mini, Llama 3 8B, Gemma 2 27B; GPT-4o and mini usually above 80% on emotion and belief tasks. Numeric SimToM deltas are not given in the text I read.
limits: Small-group preprint; no tabulated numbers read; four-choice format, chance 25%.
agent_relevance: SimToM can collapse distinct mental states in multi-agent settings; test with multi-agent items.

source: Strachan et al. (2024) Testing theory of mind in large language models and humans (Nature Human Behaviour)
finding: Battery of ToM measures (false belief, indirect requests, irony, misdirection, faux pas) on GPT and LLaMA2 families versus humans. GPT-4 at or above humans except faux pas; the failure was traced to hyperconservatism, not inference failure.
numbers: Human sample 1,907 participants. LLaMA2 beat humans on faux pas but this was illusory, a bias toward attributing ignorance.
limits: Only the abstract was read this session (Nature page needed login); no per-test numbers captured.
agent_relevance: Belief-likelihood probes separated true inference from response bias; reuse that design.

source: Hypothetical Minds (ICLR 2025) Scaffolding Theory of Mind for multi-agent tasks with LLMs
finding: An LLM agent with a Theory of Mind module that proposes natural-language hypotheses about other agents' strategies, scores them by how well they predict behaviour, and refines them. This is theory-theory style hypothesis testing inside an agent loop. Beat RL and LLM baselines in Melting Pot.
numbers: Ablation on Running with Scissors repeated: modular prompting beat a single call; adding hypothesis evaluation and refinement improved further, with returns above 10 in all scenarios; top-k=0 equals no memory of past hypotheses. Each ToM call uses 3 plus top-k LLM calls. Highest reward among LLM agents in Prisoner's Dilemma and best in 5 of 10 scenarios.
limits: Five episodes per scenario; GPT-4 far ahead of GPT-3.5 and Llama-3-70B. Hypothesis-only variant struggled against fixed strategies.
agent_relevance: Directly reusable: keep a scored list of hypotheses about another party and update from real outcomes (our G2), not from the model's own opinion.

source: Barlassina and Gordon (2017) Folk Psychology as Mental Simulation (Stanford Encyclopedia)
finding: Definition source used by the machine studies: simulation means projecting into another's perspective and running our own cognition on it. SimToM and Aoki and Kawahara adopt it as a prompt template and a mechanism hypothesis.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Not opened; cited through c01 and c24 only.
agent_relevance: Marks the definition the LLM papers use for simulation.
